acceptance_checks: A closeout carrying only the terminal state of a high-risk task is classified as a bookkeeping closeout and does not require Guardian approval.
The same closeout plus one file outside `.shiki/` is NOT classified and requires Guardian approval.
A closeout that edits any governance field of its task contract is NOT classified and requires Guardian approval.
A closeout that deletes any `.shiki` path is NOT classified.
A closeout setting a status outside the terminal set, or adding a second scorecard report, is NOT classified.
A closeout whose implementation PR is not merged is NOT classified.
An unreadable task file, a missing base snapshot, or an unresolvable implementation PR each yield NOT classified (fail closed).
A contract-mode or goal_reconcile PR is never classified as a bookkeeping closeout.
The exemption is computed only from the diff, base snapshot and live PR state: adding a label, marker or PR-body claim to a non-qualifying PR does not classify it.
tests/test_bookkeeping_closeout.py covers the positive case and every disqualifier in isolation, asserting the Guardian-requirement fallback rather than only that the PR blocks.
scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh and scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh carry the smuggling cases and stay green.
scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh stays green without being modified.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
non_goals: Exempting `.shiki`-only PRs generally, or contract-mode / goal_reconcile PRs
Letting a label, marker, PR-body claim or task field mark a PR as a bookkeeping closeout
Changing what CCA judges, the required-check set, or contract immutability
Auto-merging closeouts or authoring any approval record
Relaxing files-outside-locks, lock conflicts, or head-SHA binding
Modifying scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh or any file held by another task's lock

findings.detail: is_bookkeeping_closeout requires both --base-shiki and --merged-prs. For a normal single-task closeout PR, the cca-completion policy-check job computes MERGED_PRS only for post_merge_reconcile, and the mergegate metadata job passes neither --base-shiki nor --merged-prs, so the classifier returns False before condition 6 and the closeout still requires a second Guardian approval in prod. This matches the documented 'unfinished wiring' and is out of scope for this diff (no workflow files are among the task's changed files), but it means the task's user-facing outcome (dropping the redundant closeout approval) is not achieved by this diff alone; it depends on a follow-up that generalizes MERGED_PRS/base-snapshot to normal closeouts. The classifier logic itself is fully exercised by the tests, which pass merged_prs/base-shiki explicitly.
findings.title: Exemption is dormant in production (workflow wiring not in this diff)

test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && bash scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
title: Derive the bookkeeping-closeout exemption in MergeGate and prove it fails closed
